register.name: Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
register.detail: United Nations and partners · About 47% funded, 6 November 2026 · 20.4 million people targeted
register.text: The plan of the United Nations and its partners for life-saving aid inside Sudan in 2026, for 20.4 million of the 33.7 million people in need. It finances food, nutrition, water, health, shelter, protection and education, including US$526 million for refugees in Sudan.

register.name: WFP emergency food and nutrition
register.detail: WFP · Until April 2027 · US$426 million needed from October 2026 to March 2027
register.text: Life-saving food and nutrition assistance for 5.4 million people until April 2027. For lack of funds WFP is cutting 900,000 people from emergency food assistance until the end of 2026, and most families receive half rations.

register.name: UNICEF Humanitarian Action for Children 2026
register.detail: UNICEF · US$352.2 million mobilised by 31 August 2026 · 63% funding gap
register.note: Overlaps the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan
register.text: UNICEF’s 2026 appeal for Sudan, to reach 13.8 million people, including 7.9 million children. It finances nutrition, health, water and sanitation, and education: the standards children need first.

register.name: UK humanitarian aid for Sudan, 2026–27
register.detail: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office · Pledged 15 April 2026, Berlin · Financial year 2026–27
register.text: The UK’s humanitarian package for Sudan in 2026–27, to reach over 1.8 million people in need. It funds frontline responders and local Sudanese aid groups, including the Emergency Response Rooms, for food, water, medicine and sanitary supplies.
by: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

register.name: EU humanitarian aid for Sudan, 2026
register.detail: European Commission · Allocated in 2026 · EU contribution to the response in 2026, with neighbouring countries, €276.3 million
register.text: EU funding for life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable people inside Sudan in 2026. At the Berlin conference of 15 April 2026 the Commission pledged €360.8 million, of which €215.5 million for people in need in Sudan.

register.name: Sudan Regional Refugee Response Plan 2026
register.detail: UNHCR and 123 partners · Launched 17 February 2026 · Seven neighbouring countries
register.note: For people who fled Sudan; separate from the plan inside Sudan
register.text: Life-saving assistance in 2026 for 5.9 million people in the Central African Republic, Chad, Egypt, Ethiopia, Libya, South Sudan and Uganda. More than four million Sudanese refugees in these seven countries need urgent help.

register.name: Sudan Enhancing Community Resilience Project
register.text: Services and livelihoods for communities hit by the conflict.

register.name: Sudan Primary Education Emergency Support Project
register.text: Keeps primary schools open and children learning through the war, financed by the Global Partnership for Education.

register.name: Emergency safety nets and health (SANAD and SHARE)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved, announced 12 January 2025 · Grants to WFP, UNICEF and WHO
register.text: US$100 million of safety nets for food-insecure families and US$82 million to keep health services running, delivered by UN agencies.

register.name: Increased Coverage of Basic Health Services and Infrastructure for Internally Displaced Persons and Host Communities Project
register.detail: African Development Fund · Grant approved 30 October 2026 · Total cost $30.06 million, with $4 million from the Pandemic Fund · Delivered by UNDP
register.text: Rehabilitates and equips 20 community health centres across 11 localities in Khartoum, White Nile, Blue Nile, River Nile and Northern states, with six mobile mental health teams and vocational training. An estimated 3.1 million people benefit: the health standard for displaced families and the communities hosting them.

register.name: Emergency response operations with Islamic Relief USA
register.detail: Islamic Development Bank · Signed 19 June 2026, Baku · Two operations of US$25 million and US$7 million
register.text: An integrated emergency response for people affected by the war.

register.name: Emergency water and sanitation for Port Sudan, North and South Kordofan
register.detail: African Development Bank and UNICEF · Signed 4 June 2026 · Three stalled water projects restructured into one
register.text: Safe water for Port Sudan, the seat of government, and for Kordofan.
by: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning

register.name: Boosting Resilience of Agri-food Systems in Sudan (BOOST)
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved 22 April 2026 · Grant · Delivered by the World Food Programme
register.text: More food grown and available, and agribusiness for women and young people, in a country where war has driven hunger to record levels.

register.name: Sudan Emergency Wheat Production Project II
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved, announced 4 July 2025 · Grants · Delivered by the World Food Programme
register.text: Seed, fertiliser and support so farmers in the most fragile regions can grow the nation’s wheat.

register.name: Enhancement of Debris Management Capacity in Khartoum State
register.detail: JICA with UN-Habitat · Signed 4 November 2026 · Grant · 30 months
register.text: A Japanese grant to UN-Habitat for debris management in Khartoum, Omdurman and Karari, where the war left about 3.3 million tons of debris. Equipment, plans, training and asbestos safety help restore urban services and living conditions: the shelter standard.

register.name: REVIVE II early recovery, El Obeid
register.detail: Republic of Korea with UNDP · Announced 6 September 2026 · Additional grant; Korea’s total for REVIVE II US$8 million
register.text: Water system repairs, cash-for-work, community kitchens and bakeries, and emergency supplies in El Obeid, North Kordofan. About 48,700 people are expected to benefit directly: water, food and livelihood for displaced families.

register.name: Enhancement of Food Production Capacity for Vulnerable Farmers in River Nile State
register.detail: JICA with FAO · Signed 4 May 2026, Port Sudan · Grant of up to ¥468 million · 24 months
register.text: Seed, field equipment, irrigation repairs and training for farmers, extension officers and irrigation managers in River Nile State. It serves the food standard by raising what farmers can grow.

register.name: Proparco equity investment in Cashi
register.detail: Proparco · Equity · Reported 19 November 2026 · Proparco’s first financing operation in Sudan
register.text: Equity for the Sudanese fintech Cashi, whose MyCashi wallet has 2.2 million registered users and also works by USSD, SMS and offline card. Payments, transfers and aid distribution where cash and bank branches are scarce: the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Six tenths of the land in agriculture along the Niles: the breadbasket the nation can be again.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: The Nile dams gave six tenths of the power before the war.

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: What lies under the land already earns; the task is to turn the rent into lasting assets.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2024
items.text: Territory to farm, mine, power and protect.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 40.2% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Solar Foods
items.text: A Sudanese social enterprise that preserves farm produce with solar dryers, now working from Kassala with more than 5,000 farmers and 40 cooperatives, many led by women displaced by the war.

items.name: Al Teital Advance Industries
items.text: A Khartoum sesame-oil maker that employed 300 people before the war and is bringing its factory back.

items.name: Practical Action
items.text: Repaired sixteen solar water yards and built ten more in Kassala and Gedarif: safe water for more than 20,000 families.

items.name: Jebel Kidta
items.text: Sells and installs solar power systems, more than 1,253 so far, bringing electricity to farms, homes, schools and health clinics across Gedaref State.

items.name: Cashi
items.text: A Sudanese fintech whose MyCashi wallet, also usable by USSD, SMS and offline card, has 2.2 million registered users, with payments designed to help distribute humanitarian assistance.

items.name: Bankak
items.text: The Bank of Khartoum’s mobile banking app: salaries, money from relatives abroad and aid payments, when cash ran out.
